segments: The eighteenth dynasty:
The Arab kings.
which ancient accounts say
Alexander the Great had enclosed,
and they came out and reached Kashgar.
And they are seven kings,
with each one having seven hundred thousand horsemen.
And the name of their great king is Nasirath,
which is translated 'ruler by the command of God.'
And they are dark like Indians,
and they do not wash their faces,
nor do they comb their hair,
but they mat it like felt,
and it serves them instead of a helmet {OCR?}.
And they shoot with the bow skillfully,
and they eat plain and meager food,
and they are merciful and just,
and their horses eat meat.
And when they read the letter,
one of the Arab {OCR?} magnates said:
"This one thing is impossible,
namely, that a horse should eat meat."
And another replied:
"Do not be astonished at this,
for I have seen with my own eyes an Arab horse that eats meat and cooked fish."
But I say
that it is likely that they dry the meat,
and crush it like straw,
and feed it to the horses,
because game is abundant in that land,
and grass is scarce.
And in the year 1339 [of the Greeks, 1028 AD],
(439 of the Arabs?), a certain man of the people of Resh'aina whose name was Asfar claimed for himself
that concerning him it was said in the Quran
that he was destined to make the religion of the Arabs {Tayyaye} triumphant.
And twice he entered the territory of the Romans bandit-style,
and took captives and departed.
Then the king of the Romans wrote to Bar Marwan, the ruler:
"Between us and you there is peace,
and this bandit, if he is of your subjects,
it is right that you stop him;
and if not,
let us know so that we may take our own measures."
Then Bar Marwan summoned certain Ma'addite emirs and said:
"This Asfar is provoking the Romans against us,
and if they march out,
no rest will remain for us, nor for you.
Rather, it is right that you use a stratagem and capture him."
Then the Ma'addites went to him
and praised his zeal for the triumph of Islam {OCR: Tayyuthā}.
And he, being pleased with them,
rode out with them.
And they began racing the horses and displaying athletics {equestrian skill},
until they had gotten far from the villages.
And they laid hands on him and seized him,
and brought him to Bar Marwan,
who put irons on him and imprisoned him;
and the peace with the Romans was confirmed.
And in this year, illness multiplied and mortality intensified in the entire fourth climate,
